column3: The Hebrew dates this to the ninth day of the month without naming the month; BSB specifies the fourth month.
The Hebrew ends with a singular verb, he went by the way of the Arabah; BSB has the plural they headed toward the Arabah.
After the plural they slaughtered his sons, the Hebrew switches to singular verbs for blinding, binding, and bringing Zedekiah to Babylon; BSB keeps they throughout.
The Hebrew repeats gold and silver to distinguish the materials; BSB explicitly characterizes them as pure gold and fine silver.
The Hebrew describes latticework and pomegranates around the capital, all of bronze; BSB combines these into a network of bronze pomegranates.
The Hebrew describes five men who saw the king’s face; BSB identifies them as royal advisors.
Judah is the subject of going into exile in Hebrew; BSB expresses the exile passively.
The Hebrew says they struck Gedaliah and he died; BSB presents striking down and killing as actions of Ishmael and his companions.
The Hebrew says they arose and came to Egypt because they feared the Chaldeans; BSB explicitly calls their journey flight.
The Hebrew uses the image of lifting Jehoiachin’s head out of prison; BSB states the meaning as releasing him.
The Hebrew uses the singular “throne” of the kings; BSB uses the plural “thrones”.
The Hebrew says he ate bread continually before him; BSB makes this dining regularly at the king’s table.
The Hebrew describes the regular allowance as being given to him by the king, day by day; BSB makes the king the active subject providing a daily portion.
